compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (sm_120, Blackwell). Native fp16 tensor cores, large shared mem, 128 SMs. Problem is small per-window (16x32) so attention is bandwidth bound; MLP (32->128->32) is GEMV-like over many tokens.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Per-window attention working set is tiny: q,k,v ~ 16x32 fp16 = 1KB each. Easily fits in registers/shared. Whole block can be fused per window. MLP is the dominant FLOP portion (1x720x1280x32x128x2 = ~7.5 GFLOPs forward).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Achieving good utilization on tiny GEMMs requires careful warp-level mapping.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input/output tensor: 1*720*1280*32 fp16 = ~59 MB. Weights tiny (qkv 32*96 + proj 32*32 + fc1 32*128 + fc2 128*32 ~ 25 KB). Activations dominate BW; full fusion avoids repeated trips.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Multiple passes (norm1, attn, residual, norm2, mlp, residual) cause repeated HBM I/O if not fused.

register_pressure.notes: Per token C=32 floats fits in 32 regs. Per window 16 tokens * 32 = 512 floats which is large but tractable across a warp/block. MLP hidden=128 per token is heavier.
register_pressure.risk: Holding hidden=128 per token in regs may cause spills if not split across threads.

nodes.notes: PROBLEM: Simplified Swin block on (1,720,1280,32) fp16. window=4x4 (N=16), heads=1, dim=32, mlp_ratio=4 (hidden=128), no shift. ANALYSIS: (1) Classification: fused transformer block = LayerNorm + small attention (window-MSA) + residual + LayerNorm + MLP(GELU) + residual. Mixed elementwise + small matmul + softmax reductions. (2) Math/Deps: x1 = x + Proj(Softmax(scale*Q*K^T + RPE) * V) where (Q,K,V)=qkv(LN1(x)); x2 = x1 + fc2(GELU(fc1(LN2(x1)))). Attention is per-window independent (BW = 1*180*320 = 57600 windows). MLP/LN are per-token independent. (3) Layout: x is (B,H,W,C)=NHWC contiguous. Windows are 4x4 spatial tiles. Weights small. Reuse: each token used by qkv proj and by mlp; window tokens reused in attention. (4) Regimes: (a) attention-dominant if MLP cheap - here MLP is ~4x ops of attn; (b) memory-bound if naive multi-kernel; (c) compute-bound on MLP if fully fused. RTX5090 BW ~1.7TB/s, compute peak >100 TF fp16. With ~59MB activation, BW lower bound ~70us; reference likely 1-3ms. (5) Knobs: parallel unit (per-window vs per-token), tiling (one window per CTA, 16 threads or 1 warp), shared mem for window tile, precompute RPE constant, use tensor cores vs scalar (small matrices favor scalar/warp shuffle). (6) Skeleton: kernel grid = num_windows; each CTA loads 16x32 tile, applies LN1, computes qkv via tiny matmul, attention with softmax in registers/smem, proj, residual; then LN2, fc1 (32->128), GELU, fc2 (128->32), residual, write back. (7) FAMILIES: F1 single fused mega-kernel per window (full fusion - top candidate, working set ~16*32+16*128 fp16 = 9KB easily in smem); F2 split into two fused kernels (attention-fused, mlp-fused) sharing intermediate via global; F3 cuBLAS+custom-elementwise hybrid. Full fusion is clearly best given tiny working set.

action.description: Implement a single CUDA kernel that processes one 4x4 window per CTA. Each CTA loads 16 tokens (16x32 fp16) into shared memory, performs LN1, qkv projection (small GEMM via warp), Q*K^T (16x16) + RPE, softmax, attn*V, proj, add residual, LN2, fc1 (32->128), GELU, fc2 (128->32), add residual, write back. Use one warp (32 threads) per window: each thread handles one channel for the 16-token tile in attention path; for MLP use 32 threads to compute 128 hidden via 4-wide loop or split. Keep all intermediates in registers/shared. Avoid any global memory round-trip between sub-ops.
action.rationale: Working set per window fits trivially in shared+registers. Eliminates ~5-6 global memory passes of the 59MB activation, which dominates reference runtime. Small matmuls are easy on a warp-per-window basis.

CURRENT: does=Mega-kernel with all 4 weight matrices (qkv,proj,fc1,fc2) staged into shared memory once per CTA, then reused across WINS_PER_CTA=2 windows; per-warp computes one window via wmma. bottleneck=smem capacity / occupancy — staging ~14KB of weights + per-warp scratch limits WINS_PER_CTA, and the high static smem reduces achievable CTAs/SM vs n1a's lean version.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. Implemented qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 staged into smem with cooperative load before window loop.
UPDATE_BELIEF: Observed 3.40x vs new ref (1.72ms->2.45ms wallclock, regression from parent n1a's 5.36x/1.72ms). Caching hurt because (a) extra 14KB static smem reduced occupancy, (b) WINS_PER_CTA had to stay at 2 (4 overflowed 48KB), and (c) the original gmem weight reads were already L2/L1-cached cheaply across the grid. PERF_GAP: expected 6.5x, observed 3.4x — smem pressure dominates the saved gmem traffic. Next bet: revert weight caching for fc1/fc2 (largest), keep only qkv_w in smem if anything; or push smem reuse via dynamic smem + opt-in carveout (>48KB) to enable WINS_PER_CTA=4 with cached weights.

kernel_summary: Fuse a simplified Swin transformer block (LN1 + window-MSA(qkv,proj) + residual + LN2 + MLP(fc1,GELU,fc2) + residual) on a (1,720,1280,32) fp16 NHWC tensor with 4x4 windows (N=16), single head, hidden=128, no shift. The block is dominated by repeated activation-tensor memory traffic (~59MB) across 6+ sub-ops; weights are tiny (~25KB) and per-window working set fits easily in shared memory + registers. The natural parallel unit is one 4x4 window per CTA/warp (57600 windows total on 128 SMs of RTX5090), with dim=32 perfectly matching warp size. Key constraints: numeric tolerance rtol=atol=0.01 (fp16, slack for fused softmax/LN), correctness of softmax reduction and LN mean/var in fp32, and exposing set_params to receive state_dict in declared order including rpe_bias.
open_questions: Exact state_dict ordering after self.half() and rpe_bias buffer registration — what is the precise positional order for set_params?
Is LayerNorm's eps the default 1e-5 (in fp16 LN, accumulation should be in fp32)?
Are tensor cores worth invoking at K=32 (warp-level wmma 16x16x16 fits only one tile) or are warp-shuffle FMA loops faster for these tiny GEMMs?
Best memory layout for the 16-token window load — gather via 16 strided loads of 32 fp16 each, or transpose to per-window contiguous in a tiny pre-pass?
Do we need to support arbitrary H,W or hard-code the 720x1280 case (nH=180, nW=320, both divisible by 4)?
Will fc1 weights (32x128 = 4KB fp16) and fc2 (128x32 = 4KB fp16) fit comfortably as __constant__ memory or be cached in L1 across all CTAs?
Acceptable approximation for GELU (tanh-approx vs exact erf) under the 0.01 tolerance?
Is the residual path's add-into-output stable in fp16, or do we need fp32 accumulation to stay within tolerance?
